label: Clerical elector title
summary: Each active clerical elector title of the faith that currently has a holder.
details: Runs on a faith. The items are titles. Vanilla uses it for the holders of these titles, for example to add them to a list or to the Christian Church situation as participants.

label: Elector title in region
summary: Every clerical elector title that lies within a clerical region.
details: Runs on a title and gives titles. The game documents only the words 'within clerical region', so which region it means (presumably the title it runs on) is not stated. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Clerical region in title
summary: Each clerical region that has counties inside the de jure title it runs on.
details: The items are titles; a clerical region is a title in the game's data. Vanilla only looks at the holder of such a region inside it.

label: Clerical region in realm
summary: Each clerical region that the game links to the character's realm.
details: The game's documentation is worded like the de jure title version (and has a typo), so it does not say exactly how the realm decides which regions count. Vanilla uses it once, to look at the region's holder.

label: Clerical region
summary: Each clerical region title of the faith.
details: Runs on a faith. Vanilla often sorts these by the holder's piety level and takes the first one or few. It also uses it to hand every region holder to the Christian Church situation.

label: Close family member
summary: Each close relative of the character: father, mother, siblings, children and grandparents.
details: Vanilla uses it a lot to give opinions, collect relatives into lists and pass on a culture change. The random form in vanilla sometimes writes `even_if_dead = yes` to include dead relatives; the game does not say what happens without it.

fields.name: even_if_dead
fields.text: Vanilla writes this in the random form to include relatives who have died.

label: Close or extended relative
summary: Each close or extended relative of the character: parents, siblings, children, grandparents, uncles and aunts, nephews and nieces, and cousins.
details: It is the wider version of the close family list. Vanilla uses it to find relatives to convert, to notify of bastardy, or to give opinions to.

fields.name: even_if_dead
fields.text: Vanilla writes this to include relatives who have died.

label: Combat side
summary: Both sides of the combat, the attacker and the defender.
details: Runs on a combat. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Completed legend
summary: Every legend in the world that has been completed.
details: It does not need a scope to run in. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Concubine
summary: Each concubine of the character.
details: Spouses are not included; use the consort list for both. Vanilla uses it to remove a concubine, to add them to lists, or to check them.

label: Confederation
summary: Every confederation in the game.
details: A confederation has member houses (the app calls it a house confederation). It does not need a scope to run in. Vanilla uses the check form to find the confederation led by a house whose head serves a given top liege.

label: Confederation member
summary: Each character who is a member of the confederation.
details: Vanilla uses it to make members join a faction, to change their government, and to collect them into lists.

label: Member house
summary: Each house that is a member of the confederation.
details: Vanilla uses it to run effects on the houses and their heads, and to count them (for example a limit on how many houses there are).

label: Confederation type
summary: Every confederation type defined in the game.
details: This goes through the type definitions, not through running confederations. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Connected county
summary: Each county that is connected to this county, based on the top liege.
details: The game's documentation shows two optional settings for the connection (a sea distance and a one-county land gap) but does not say more about what counts as connected. Vanilla uses it to find counties cut off from the rest of a realm.

fields.name: max_naval_distance
fields.text: Going by its name, the longest sea distance a connection may cross.
fields.values: a number (vanilla uses 2000, the game's documentation shows 500)

fields.name: allow_one_county_land_gap
fields.text: Going by its name, allows a gap of one county on land.

fields.name: invert
fields.text: Vanilla writes `invert = yes` when collecting disconnected counties; the game documents nothing about it.

label: Consort
summary: Each consort of the character, meaning each spouse and each concubine.
details: Vanilla uses it a lot: to find the partners, give them opinions, and save one as a scope.

fields.name: even_if_dead
fields.text: Vanilla uses it in checks to include a dead consort.

label: Contact
summary: Each contact character of the character.
details: The game does not explain what makes a character a contact. Vanilla uses it with hooks, for example to find who holds a favor hook on the character.

label: Contribution
summary: Each contribution of the great project, whether it has been funded or not.
details: Vanilla uses it to send an event to each contributor, to find an unfunded required contribution, and to check whether one is funded.

label: Controlled faith
summary: Each faith that is headed by the title.
details: Runs on a title. Vanilla only uses the check form, comparing against a given faith or religion.

label: Title regiment
summary: Each men-at-arms regiment that belongs to the title.
details: Vanilla uses it once, to check whether a regiment is raised.

label: Councillor
summary: Each councillor of the character.
details: Vanilla uses it a lot, picking one by skill or opinion, or checking if one of them passes the kurultai trigger.

label: County
summary: Every county in the game.
details: It does not need a scope to run in. Vanilla uses it for world-wide effects, such as setting variables or a faith or rite on counties.

label: County holy site
summary: Each holy site in the county.
details: Vanilla uses it to look at the faiths of a holy site, its artifact, and who controls its barony.

label: County in clerical region
summary: Each county that lies within the clerical region.
details: Runs on a clerical region title. Vanilla uses it to set rites, add county modifiers and gather counties of a given rite.

label: County in region
summary: Each county in the region you name inside it.
details: The region has to be written in the block. It does not need a scope to run in.

fields.name: region
fields.text: The geographical region whose counties are listed.

label: County province
summary: Each province of the county.
details: Vanilla uses it for province modifiers, holdings and buildings.

label: County epidemic
summary: Each epidemic affecting the provinces of the county.
details: You can filter by how strong the outbreak is by writing an intensity in the block.

fields.name: intensity
fields.text: Filters the epidemics by outbreak intensity.
fields.values: an intensity such as apocalyptic; vanilla also writes a comparison like `>= major`

label: County situation
summary: Each situation that the county is part of.
details: Vanilla uses it to find natural disasters in a county and to trigger a catalyst on them.

label: County situation sub-region
summary: Each sub-region of a situation that the county is part of.
details: Vanilla uses it to check the sub-region's current phase.

label: County struggle
summary: Each struggle that the county is part of.
details: Vanilla only uses the check form, to test the struggle's type or its phase parameters.

label: Position candidate
summary: Each character who is a valid candidate for the court position type you name.
details: The game's documentation names the field `court_position`, but the one vanilla use writes `court_position_type`, so check which one your game version accepts.

fields.name: court_position_type
fields.text: The court position the candidates are for. The game's documentation calls it `court_position`.
fields.values: a court position type or a saved scope of one

label: Position employer
summary: Each character who employs the character in any court position.
details: Vanilla only uses the check form, to compare against a character.

label: Position holder
summary: Each character the character employs in the court position.
details: The game's documentation says the type is optional. Vanilla mostly names a type and saves the holder as a scope, for example a jester or an antiquarian.

fields.name: type
fields.text: Only holders of this court position.
fields.values: a court position type or a saved scope of one

label: Court position type
summary: Every court position type defined in the game.
details: This goes through the type definitions, not through who holds them. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Courtier
summary: Each courtier of the character's court.
details: Vanilla uses it heavily: giving opinions and traits, collecting them in lists, picking by a skill or age.

label: Absent courtier
summary: Each courtier of the character who is away.
details: Vanilla uses it to change the faith or rite of such courtiers and collect them in a list.

label: Courtier or guest
summary: Each courtier and each guest, including those from the pool and from foreign courts.
details: It is wider than the courtier list. Vanilla uses it for opinions, lists and finding someone available.

label: County of the culture
summary: Each county of the culture.
details: Vanilla uses it to collect counties by region into lists, and in checks by terrain or the share of counties.

label: Culture duchy
summary: Each duchy that has at least one county of the culture.
details: Vanilla uses it in the check form, to exclude a duchy or match its region, and once in the random form to save a duchy.

label: Culture empire
summary: Each empire that has at least one county of the culture.
details: Vanilla uses only the check form, to see whether the empire's counties belong to a given top liege.

label: Culture
summary: Every culture in the game.
details: It does not need a scope to run in. Vanilla uses it to pick a culture as a scope and to check cultural era or acceptance.

label: Culture hegemony
summary: Each hegemony that has at least one county of the culture.
details: Vanilla does not use it.

label: Culture innovation
summary: Every culture innovation defined in the game.
details: This goes through the definitions, not the innovations a culture has learned. Vanilla uses it to pick one by random.

label: Culture kingdom
summary: Each kingdom that has at least one county of the culture.
details: Vanilla uses only the check form, to see whether the kingdom's counties belong to a given top liege.

label: Culture pillar
summary: Every culture pillar defined in the game.
details: This goes through the definitions, not the pillars a culture has chosen. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Culture tradition
summary: Every culture tradition defined in the game.
details: This goes through the definitions, not the traditions a culture has. Vanilla uses it once, only to count them.

label: De jure claim
summary: Each title the character has a de jure claim to.
details: Vanilla uses it to pick one claim and to compare against a saved title.

label: De jure county
summary: Each county that lies within the de jure title.
details: De jure means by the map's own borders, whoever holds them now. Vanilla uses it a lot: county modifiers, control, changing holders and lists.

label: De jure county holder
summary: Each character who directly holds a county within the de jure title.
details: Vanilla uses it to collect holders, order them, and test landed or independent rulers.

label: De jure top liege
summary: Each top liege of the counties within the de jure title.
details: Vanilla only uses the check form, to compare with a saved character.
